clue.text: Ploughman's enquiry having sowed his seed?

definitions.text: Ploughman's enquiry having sowed his seed?

parts.words: Ploughman's enquiry having sowed his seed?
parts.note: a farmer's question after sowing reads, cryptically, as the bedroom question a lover asks after the act

explanation.surface: A farmer, having sown his field, asks a question about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ploughing and sowing are a coy picture of sex; the question is the cliché asked afterwards, which also fits a ploughman who has just turned the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock post-coital query, and a ploughman has literally just shifted the soil.

clue.text: Mark out shop, then university

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Instructions to mark out the boundary of a shop and then a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark out the limits of something is to set its boundaries, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Rare delivery is among one of seven on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits on top of the next
among means the word is goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a day is one of the seven in a week
taken as written
a cutter is a small fast sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A rare consignment arrives aboard one of seven ships.
explanation.walkthrough: A daisy-cutter is a cricket ball (or bowling delivery) that skims along the ground; it is rare at a decent level, hence 'Rare delivery'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball bowled so low it rolls along the turf is called by this name, an uncommon delivery.

clue.text: "Meat" misspelt "meet" or an abnormality in the extreme

parts.note: ham is a kind of meat

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of the words that follow are written in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pedant notes that 'meat' was misspelt 'meet', calling it an extreme abnormality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' rearranges MEET OR into MERTOE. 'the extreme' is a body extremity, the toe.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a deformity in which a toe bends permanently, so a malformation at a bodily extremity.

clue.text: Abstinent church admitted to wine consumption at first

indicators.note: admitted to means one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A self-denying churchman lets himself into wine drinking, at least to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic person practises severe self-denial, so the adjective is close to abstemious.

clue.text: See 19 across
Pass out after injection into sensitive area, as one moaning

indicators.note: after injection into means the scrambled piece is placed inside the body part

parts.note: the crotch is a tender part of the body

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word pass are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone faints after a jab in a tender spot and groans about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting, but 'out' is the anagram signal on PASS; 'sensitive area' is the groin.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, irritable person who complains is called by this informal name.

clue.text: Compound contains iodine for conductor

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: this compound includes iodine, used as a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' rearranges CONTAINS plus I. 'conductor' suggests electricity but means the Italian maestro Arturo Toscanini.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: See 2
Most are rough to some extent, one looking hard

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A general observation that most people are rough round the edges, made by a hard-eyed observer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gazes fixedly at another is looking hard, the literal sense of a starer.

clue.text: Toilet rolls, about a thousand, providing theme

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
rolls means the letters of the word toilet tumble into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
providing means if, as a condition

explanation.surface: Toilet rolls, a thousand of them, supplying a recurring theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' rearranges TOILET into LEITOT, which goes 'about' M.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring musical or literary motif attached to an idea or character.

clue.text: Prepared to act? Start

definitions.meaning: an actor ready to perform is in place on the stage set, read as two words

explanation.surface: A stage prompt: ready to perform? Begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is the beginning of something, and read as two words describes a performer in position.

clue.text: See 14
Control, say, put back

parts.note: to rein something in is to control it
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take control, say, and put things back.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a person or thing to a former position is to put them back.

clue.text: Rat or rat — it could be?

definitions.note: a rat is slang for a betrayer or informer

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is it a rat or something rattish?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first 'Rat'; 'could be' rearranges OR RAT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for someone who betrays his comrades, a turncoat.

clue.text: Open or closed, perhaps

parts.note: a case can be open or closed, and the phrase also means whichever applies

explanation.surface: Something is either open or shut, depending.
explanation.walkthrough: Open and closed are both states a case (legal or a box) can be in, and the phrase means 'whichever applies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means depending on circumstances, and the case itself could be open or closed.

clue.text: Sow seed, hoeing extensively, planting in gaps at each opening

indicators.note: at each opening takes the initial letter of every word in the stretch

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: sow seed, hoeing widely, putting it into gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' looks like a verb in a gardening tip, but it is the noun, a female pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow is an adult female pig, which can be described plainly as a female swine.

clue.text: See 1 across
Drive home, referring to signs at the borders on the way

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: at the borders takes just the outer letters of the word signs

explanation.surface: Driving home, referring to the road signs along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to emphasise it strongly, which is to lay weight on it.

clue.text: Run, as one jumping

definitions.meaning: to captain a team or ship is to run it
a person hopping along or jumping rope

explanation.surface: Running as someone who leaps along.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain runs a team or boat, and someone who hops and bounds also takes this name.

clue.text: Soldier back at the front — tasteless pretension matters overseas

parts.note: fore means at the front

indicators.note: back means the soldier's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
naff is British slang for tacky or tasteless
putting on airs is pretentious behaviour

explanation.surface: A soldier returns to the front and rails at the tacky showing-off he finds abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GI into IG. NAFF is British slang for cheap and tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings with other countries are the international concerns a government handles abroad.

clue.text: See 1 across
No place for art, direct header scored

parts.note: taken as written
the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: header means the top letter of direct, which heads it in a down clue

explanation.surface: A football report: no room for flair, the direct header scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks like a goal from the header but means written in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is scored has been written down in notation.

clue.text: Belief under leadership of Salmond in diatribe

indicators.note: under means, in a down clue, this piece goes beneath the next
leadership of takes the leading letter of Salmond

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: A political belief expressed under Alex Salmond's leadership in a rant.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Salmond led the Scottish National Party; only his initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, tiresome harangue or tirade, much like a diatribe.

clue.text: French singer, singer keeping alive, surprisingly

indicators.note: keeping means the singer holds the next piece inside

parts.note: Cher is an American pop singer

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters of alive appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One singer, surprisingly, keeping another alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'singer' is deliberate: the first belongs to the definition, the second is Cher, who 'keeping' holds the anagram ('surprisingly') of the word alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Chevalier was a celebrated French entertainer and vocalist.

clue.text: Result of fire, bum full of gas

indicators.note: full of means the gas goes inside the other piece

parts.note: ass is slang for the backside
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: A crude joke: fire comes from a backside full of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left after burning is the powdery residue of combustion.

clue.text: Brave attempt in the end to get lost

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, here one of the Hopi people

indicators.note: in the end takes just the final letter of attempt

explanation.surface: A courageous effort that ends with getting lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive British slang ordering someone to go away.

clue.text: See 5
Chase fraudulent online buyer

indicators.note: fraudulent suggests the word chase is a fake, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Pursue a fraudster shopping on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic money is what pays for purchases made over the internet, so it buys online.

clue.text: Copy letters capturing passionate heart of relative

indicators.note: capturing means the mail holds the next piece inside

parts.note: letters arrive in the post, the mail
hot means passionate

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letters of relative

explanation.surface: Copied letters reveal a passionate love for a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A Photostat is a photographic duplicate of a document, made by an early copying machine.

clue.text: Furniture item, one in theatre?

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for crockery
a backstage helper who clothes the actors

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture found in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a kitchen cupboard with shelves and the wardrobe assistant who dresses performers.

clue.text: The way builder's helper joins police

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
a hod is the trough a labourer uses to carry bricks

explanation.surface: A building labourer's mate joins the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a procedure or manner of doing something, a way.
